note: GLOBALCIT's Citizenship Law Dataset v3.0 (EUI, 2025), coding the law in force on 1 January 2024 (A06a OMA 15; A06b OMA 15; L05 OMA 5, OMA 19): ordinary naturalisation after 20 years' residence; the applicant must give up other citizenships; a citizen loses the citizenship on voluntarily taking another. Reforms after that date are checked in the file's later sources, where a later source is given. Citizenship at birth is read from the same dataset's 2024 coding of modes A01a (descent, born in country: Gender restriction: no or restricted access if the mother is a citizen (wedlock condition/supplementary provision may apply)), A01b (descent, born abroad: Gender restriction: no or restricted access if the mother is a citizen (wedlock condition/supplementary provision may apply)), A02a (birth in country: No provision) and A02b (birth in country to a parent born there: No provision), as its codebook (RSC/GLOBALCIT 2025/01, sections 3.2.1a to 3.2.2b) defines them: not by birth in the territory alone (provisions for foundlings and children otherwise stateless, modes A03a and A03b, aren't held by the form); by descent from the father only, a child born abroad on the limit the dataset states. Changes to the law at birth after 1 January 2024 weren't checked for this file.

sources.said: Person has been resident in Oman for at least 20 years. ... Written consent and proof of renunciation of citizenship of another country required. ... Person has acquired a foreign citizenship without prior permission of the authorities. ... Gender restriction: no or restricted access if the mother is a citizen (wedlock condition/supplementary provision may apply) ... Person is born in Oman to a male citizen. Person born to a female citizen can only obtain citizenship when the father was a citizen who became stateless or if the father is unknown.; Person is the child of a male citizen who has deceased or abandoned or divorced his wife at least 10 years ago and he/she had resided in the country for at least 10 years. Other conditions: good character, not convicted of crime or offence in breach of trust or honor, written consent and proof of renunciation of citizenship of another country, written consent of guardian. ...
